labels.label: cex:start_singular_manifold_homeomorphic
labels.notes: Unmarked in all three modules and partial in the REPORT, which is correct: two tagged sorrys under DEC-136. DEFINITIONS ARE THE REAL ONES. (i) SpecialOrth V is the subgroup of linear isometries with det = 1. It acts on RaySphere V = sphere(0,1) by restriction. Rigidity is genuine: two linear maps that agree on an open subset of the sphere agree on the open cone over it, whose affine span is everything. Faithfulness is proved. Euc4 = ℝ ⊕ (ℝ ⊕ ℂ) with the L² inner product, and euc4Isometry is an isometry onto EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4), so SO4/Sph3 is SO(4)/𝕊³. (ii) C_θ = Γ₁\𝔻_∞ ≅ ℂ, developed by (r,φ) ↦ stereoInv(r e^{iθφ}), with φ of period 1. The round metric 4|dv|²/(1+|v|²)² pulls back to dρ² + sin²ρ θ²dφ² with ρ = 2 arctan r ∈ [0,π): the spherical cone of angle θ. The structure is the unique maximal a.e. atlas for which the projection is an a.e. morphism; no field is involved. 'Apex singular iff θ ≠ 2π' (polarCone, SphCone.apex_mem_sing_iff) is a real proof. A chart at the apex together with deck invariance forces e^{iα} = 1. Then α = 2πm with m ≥ 2 makes the chart non-injective (angles 0 and 1/m). For α = 2π an explicit global chart is built. (iii) IsConePoint θ x is exactly the library's HasXAType for (SphCone, S_θ = {apex}), that is an XAChart: U open ∋ x, V open and connected in C_θ, φ : U ≃ₜ V an a.e. morphism, φ x = apex. This matches def:atlas (l.1905). It is non-vacuous for every θ (isConePoint_apex). (iv) Angle uniqueness is genuine. sphCone_exists_int_mul lifts the isomorphism on a punctured strip through exp : ℂ → ℂ* (mathlib's covering lift). It compares the developing maps by rigidity on the strip, shows that the comparing element fixes the north pole (by a limit along a ray) and is therefore a rotation about the axis, and reads off an integer-valued continuous function and the deck translation, giving θ = kθ'. sphCone_eq_of_iso applies this both ways, using that a.e. isomorphisms preserve Sing, and IsConePoint.angle_eq restricts both charts to a connected component. (v) IsConeSphere has the fields M ≃ₜ 𝕊², p injective, θ_i > 0, p_i a cone point of angle θ_i, and Sing ⊆ range p. That is the definition, not a conclusion. IsConeSphere.sing_eq and isConePoint_iff are proved from it. Its only witness is the round 𝕊² with s = 0. No IsConeSphere with a genuine cone point is built (a football would be the cheap one); this is left to T-gx-troyanov by DEC-136. THE STATEMENT. TroyanovTheorem is the paper's citation (l.1930): every θ satisfying DEC-69's TroyanovAngleCondition (s ≥ 3, verbatim) admits a cone sphere with these angles. TroyanovAngleCondition.subcritical is correct. With χ = χ'/2π and θ_i = 2π(1+β_i), MR1005085's 0 < χ < min(2, 2+2 min β_i) reads 0 < χ' < min(4π, 2θ_i). The paper's χ' ≤ θ_j < 2θ_j gives the second bound. χ' = 4π would force every θ_j ≥ 4π, so χ' ≥ 4π + 2πs > 4π, a contradiction. The recollection of MR1005085 is disclosed as unchecked and agrees with mine. TroyanovTheorem is weaker than MR1005085 itself (S² only, the paper's narrower condition, conformal class and positions not prescribed); it is exactly what the cex uses. ThurstonSuspensionFacts asserts, for every cone sphere with Troyanov angles that are pairwise distinct, (a) Sing(susp Σ) = O ∪ the open rays over the p_i with θ_i ≠ 2π, and (b) DEC-69's SuspensionCexFacts at O. I checked that this is true mathematically, so it is not a vacuous or false target. Rays over angles θ_i ∉ 2πℤ have non-trivial rotational holonomy. Over θ_i ∈ 2πℤ, θ_i ≥ 4π, the developing map is a branched cover, hence not injective. O lies in the closure of at least 3 singular rays. rigid: φ(O) = O, because at O Sing is a star with at least 3 arms, while on a ray it is an arc. φ preserves the distance to O and therefore induces an orientation-preserving isometry of Σ fixing the at least 3 genuine cone points, which have distinct angles that are invariants. Such an isometry is the identity, by Kerékjártó or by the 2 fixed points of an S¹-action. Then φ = id on U₁ by rigidity. rot: the local rotations about a singular ray are not restrictions of automorphisms, since Aut is trivial. TroyanovSuspensionTheoremS3 = ∃ Σ with IsConeSphere Σ θ p ∧ ThurstonCexFacts θ p. It is tied to θ through the angles at the p_i (invariants, proved) and through sing_eq. troyanovSuspensionTheoremS3_of, TroyanovSuspensionTheoremS3.troyanovSuspensionTheorem (⇒ GX.TroyanovSuspensionTheorem SO4 Sph3, witness susp Σ and O = mk(p_0, 0)) and cex_start_singular_manifold_homeomorphic_S3 are all sorry-free, with the Prop taken as a hypothesis. The last one concludes the paper's 'for S ⊆ sing(M), (M,S) analytic iff S = {O}', plus '(M, sing M) not analytic'. The omission of Aut(Σ) ≅ Aut(M) is disclosed (SCOPE (a), question 4). FINDINGS CHECKED, BOTH TRUE. (1) (9π/10, 19π/20, π, 2π): Σ(θ_i − 2π) + 4π = 17π/20 ≤ 18π/20 = min. It satisfies the printed condition with pairwise distinct angles, and an angle 2π is a regular point. The condition forces at least 3 angles ≠ 2π (card 0, 1, 2 each contradict χ' ≤ θ_j); this is proved. (2) At l.698–700, r ranges over ℝ₊ and sin²(π) = 0, so ĝ degenerates at r = π and the closed version has a second centre. The wording overstates (minor finding 2). READINGS: r ∈ [0,π), the X_θ-chart notion of a conical singularity, 'generic' as pairwise distinct (DEC-69), and Aut omitted. All four are recorded as questions, and none makes a statement vacuous.

findings.what: Finding 2 is true but overstated in one clause. 'As printed it is not a Riemannian metric locally isometric to S^{n+1} beyond r < π' suggests failure for every r ≥ π. In fact ĝ = dr² + sin²r g degenerates only on r ∈ πℤ_{>0}, and on each open band (kπ, (k+1)π) it is again locally spherical on rays over regular points. The defect is that with r ∈ ℝ₊ the printed ĝ is not a Riemannian metric at all, because the r = π level collapses. The author will read this as a fact about the paper, so the clause should be exact.
findings.fix: Reword: 'with r over ℝ₊, ĝ degenerates at r = π (and every kπ), so (M × ℝ₊)/∼ with ĝ is not a Riemannian (cone-)manifold; the intended model is r ∈ [0, π) (one centre) or [0, π] with both ends collapsed (two centres).'

findings.what: IsConePoint is presented as 'gx's HasXAType (def:atlas, l.1905) for the family (C_θ) with S_θ = {apex}'. In the Lean library this is correct: HasXAType asks no analyticity. But def:atlas is stated for an analytic family of model spaces (def:family_singular_manifolds_endowed, l.1899), and (C_θ)_{θ>0} with S_θ = {apex} is not one. S_{2π} = {apex} is not contained in sing(C_{2π}) = ∅ (SphCone.sing_eq_empty), and the exists_aut half is not proved even for θ ≠ 2π. SCOPE (c) discloses the first point and SCOPE (d) the second, but separately, and neither says that IsConePoint therefore lies outside def:atlas's standing hypothesis. Nothing is over-claimed in Lean.
findings.fix: One sentence in SCOPE (a): 'the family (C_θ)_{θ>0}, S_θ = {apex}, is not an analytic family in the sense of l.1899 (S_{2π} ⊄ sing C_{2π}; exists_aut unproved): IsConePoint is the chart condition of def:atlas without its standing hypothesis; restricted to θ ≠ 2π, the eq_of_iso half is sphCone_eq_of_iso.'
